summary: Add confident-primary fallback rule to skip secondary expert routing when primary clearly wins
rationale: Current top-2 routing sends almost all traffic remotely (0.9995 ratio) with poor load balance (CV=3.94)
Secondary routes with low confidence contribute little value but consume capacity and communication
Confident-primary fallback skips secondary when primary score > 0.80 or score gap > 0.20
This reduces tokens_rerouted and estimated_a2a_bytes while preserving model quality
Low-risk localized change that keeps top-2 as default behavior
expected_effects: Reduce tokens_rerouted by skipping weak secondary routes
Lower estimated_a2a_bytes due to fewer secondary token dispatches
Improve load_balance_cv by reducing contention on secondary expert capacity
Achieve 8-15% step_time improvement from reduced communication
Keep tokens_dropped stable or slightly reduced
risks: May slightly reduce model expressiveness for ambiguous tokens
Confidence thresholds may need tuning for different workloads
Could increase tokens_dropped if capacity is too tight
